items.stem: The first stage of 2SLS regresses:
options: each endogenous RHS regressor on the full instrument set
the outcome on the endogenous regressors
the structural residuals on fitted values
items.explanation: Each endogenous structural regressor is projected onto the full set of exogenous instruments.

items.stem: The instrument matrix Z includes:
options: included exogenous controls and excluded instruments
items.explanation: Included exogenous controls instrument themselves and belong in Z.

items.stem: The second stage regresses Y on:
options: included exogenous controls and fitted endogenous regressors
items.explanation: The second-stage structural regression retains the included controls and replaces endogenous regressors by their fitted values.

items.stem: If the reduced-form slope is 3 and the first-stage slope is 1.5, the just-identified 2SLS estimate is:
items.explanation: The just-identified 2SLS coefficient is the reduced-form slope divided by the first-stage slope: 3/1.5=2.

items.stem: The projection matrix onto the instrument space is:
items.explanation: The matrix P_Z projects vectors onto the column space of Z when Z has full column rank.

items.stem: In the just-identified one-instrument case, 2SLS equals:
items.explanation: With one endogenous regressor and one valid excluded instrument, 2SLS reduces to the reduced-form/first-stage ratio.

items.stem: The matrix 2SLS estimator is:
items.explanation: The projection matrix P_Z replaces the ordinary OLS projection in the cross-products.

items.stem: For Z=(−1,0,1) and X=(1,2,4), the first-stage slope of X on Z is:
items.explanation: The centred cross-product is 3 and the instrument sum of squares is 2, so the slope is 3/2.

items.stem: If W is an included exogenous control, the first-stage instrument matrix should:
options: include W along with excluded instruments
omit W because it is not excluded
replace W by the fitted outcome
items.explanation: All included exogenous regressors belong in Z, even though they are not excluded instruments.

items.stem: Why is the fitted endogenous regressor used in stage two?
options: it isolates the component predicted by exogenous instruments
it makes the structural disturbance normal
items.explanation: The first-stage projection retains the instrument-predicted component of the endogenous regressor.

items.stem: For the same data, Y=(2,5,8) and Z=(−1,0,1), the reduced-form slope is:
items.explanation: The centred cross-product is 6 and S_ZZ=2, so the reduced-form slope is 3.

items.stem: Naive second-stage OLS standard errors are generally:
options: valid only when the first stage is strong
not the correct final 2SLS standard errors
items.explanation: The second-stage fitted regressors are generated; the covariance calculation must use the 2SLS formula.

items.stem: The first-stage regression for each endogenous regressor uses:
options: the same full instrument matrix Z
a different excluded instrument chosen after seeing Y
items.explanation: Every endogenous regressor is projected onto the same full exogenous instrument set.

items.stem: Which statements about 2SLS are correct? A. Included exogenous controls belong in Z. B. Only excluded instruments belong in Z. C. Stage two uses fitted endogenous regressors. D. Naive second-stage OLS SE are always correct.
items.explanation: A and C are true. The full instrument set includes included exogenous controls, and the second stage uses fitted endogenous regressors.
statements: Included exogenous controls belong in Z
Only excluded instruments belong in Z
Stage two uses fitted endogenous regressors
Naive second-stage OLS SE are always correct

A.why: This follows from the standard 2SLS construction.

B.why: This confuses the excluded-instrument subset with the full instrument matrix.

C.why: This follows from the standard 2SLS construction.

D.why: This is not a valid general conclusion about 2SLS.

items.stem: If the instruments are weak, 2SLS may be:
options: imprecise and unreliable in finite samples
items.explanation: Weak first-stage relationships make IV estimates unstable and can undermine conventional inference.

items.stem: For the worked example, reduced-form slope 3 divided by first-stage slope 1.5 gives:
items.explanation: The just-identified 2SLS estimate is 3/1.5=2.

items.stem: If a reduced-form coefficient is 0.84 and the first-stage coefficient is 0.28, the 2SLS estimate is:
items.explanation: The ratio is 0.84/0.28=3; the first-stage effect converts the instrument's outcome effect into an effect per unit X.

items.stem: Which statements about the 2SLS matrix estimator are correct? A. P_Z is symmetric. B. P_Z is generally not idempotent. C. P_Z is idempotent. D. P_Z projects onto the column space of X.
items.explanation: A and C are true. P_Z is a symmetric idempotent projection onto the instrument space, not generally the column space of X.
statements: P_Z projects onto the column space of X

items.stem: The conventional homoscedastic 2SLS covariance matrix is:
items.explanation: Under homoscedastic disturbances, the conventional covariance uses the projected cross-product matrix X′P_ZX.

items.stem: For the 3-point example, the Wald ratio from reduced-form slope 3 and first-stage slope 3/2 is:
items.explanation: 3 divided by 3/2 equals 2. This is the just-identified 2SLS estimate.
